args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the v2.3.1 deploy, with error rate at ~18%. Current state was v2.3.1 in all regions, healthy=false.

Remediation: rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with healthy status in production (v2.2.9 healthy at seq 0, v2.3.0 healthy at seq 1, v2.3.1 unhealthy at seq 3; v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy).

The first rollback attempt partially failed — the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout to v2.3.0 in all three production regions.

Post-rollback verification: all production regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate ~0.2%.

Follow-up needed: root-cause analysis on the v2.3.1 change before any re-deploy attempt; note v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so redeploying it would require change-manager approval.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done. Here's what happened:

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), `healthy: false`, error rate ~18%. Release history showed v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy). The most recent release healthy *in production* was **v2.3.0** — I deliberately excluded v2.3.1-rc, which was staging-only and also unhealthy.

**Rollback:** The first attempt failed partway — `partial_failure: rollout halted after us-east` — leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). I verified the actual regional state rather than assuming, then retried, which completed the rollout to v2.3.0 in all regions. Post-rollback check confirms all three regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2, checkout-api). Note: the create call returned a 30000ms timeout, so I listed incidents before retrying — the incident had in fact been created, so I did not re-submit and no duplicate page was sent. The summary documents the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback target and reasoning, the partial-failure/retry sequence, and post-rollback verification.

**One thing to flag for follow-up:** v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production. Per policy, any future attempt to deploy it requires change-manager approval — that's captured in the incident summary, and root-cause analysis is needed before anyone tries. The rollback itself needed no approval, since v2.3.0 has a prior healthy production history.
